# Sirach Chapter 18 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 18 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_018_page_001.jpg

---

**18:1** He who lives forever created the whole universe;

**18:2** the LORD alone is righteous.

**18:3** He steers the world with the span of his hand, and all things obey his will; for he is king of all things by his power, separating among them the holy things from the profane.

**18:4** He gave no one the power to declare his works; and who can trace his mighty deeds?

**18:5** Who can measure the might of his majesty? And who can extend his hand to recount his mercies?

**18:6** It is not possible to diminish or increase, and it is not possible to trace the wonders of the LORD.

**18:7** When a human being finishes, he is just beginning; and when he stops, he will be perplexed.

**18:8** What is a human being, and what is the use of him? What is his good, and what is his evil?

**18:9** The number of a man's days, at most, is a hundred years.

**18:10** Like a drop of water from the sea and a grain of sand — so are these few years compared to the age of eternity.

**18:11** Therefore the LORD is patient with them and pours out his mercy upon them.

**18:12** He sees and recognizes that their end is evil, therefore he multiplies his forgiveness.

**18:13** The compassion of a person is toward his neighbor, but the compassion of the LORD is upon all flesh; reproving, disciplining, teaching, and turning them back as a shepherd does his flock.

**18:14** He has compassion on those who receive discipline and who are zealous in his ordinances.

**18:15** My child, do not mix reproach with your good deeds, nor bitter words with any of your gifts.

**18:16** Does not dew relieve the heat? So a word is better than a gift.

**18:17** Indeed, does not a word surpass a good gift? But both are found with a gracious man.

**18:18** A fool is ungracious and abusive, and a gift from a grudging person makes the eyes weep.

**18:19** Before you speak, learn; and before you fall ill, care for your health.

**18:20** Before judgment comes, examine yourself; and in the hour of visitation you will find forgiveness.

**18:21** Before falling ill, humble yourself; and at the time of sinning, show repentance.

**18:22** Let nothing hinder you from paying a vow in due time, and do not wait until death to be released from it.

**18:23** Before making a vow, prepare yourself; and do not be as one who tests the LORD.

**18:24** Think of the wrath at the end of days, and the hour of punishment in the turning away of his face.

**18:25** In the time of plenty, think of want; and in the days of wealth, think of poverty and need.

**18:26** From morning to evening the time changes; and all things pass quickly before the LORD.

**18:27** The wise person is cautious in all things; and in days of sinning, he guards against foolish behavior.

**18:28** Every intelligent person knows wisdom, and gives thanks to the one who found her.

**18:29** Those who understand sayings have also shown wisdom, and have poured out fitting proverbs.

**18:30** Do not go after your lusts, but restrain your cravings.

**18:31** If you give your soul its desires, it will make you the laughingstock of your enemies.

**18:32** Do not delight in luxury, lest you become impoverished by it.

**18:33** Do not make yourself a beggar by feasting with borrowed money, when you have nothing in your purse.
